title: Naive Bayes machine-learning score predicts 30-day mortality in COVID-19 pneumonia
summary: A naive Bayes classifier with forward feature search produced a six-feature score (age, MCHC, PaO2/FiO2, temperature, prior stroke, sex) for 30-day mortality in 852 patients with COVID-19 pneumonia. The AUC was 0.78 internally and 0.79 on an external cohort of 86 patients at a second Italian centre, comparable to the 4C score. The study is retrospective and the external cohort is small with wide confidence intervals.
ai_technology: Naive Bayes classifier with forward feature search

evidence.tested: Internal test cohort and external validation on 86 patients at Centro Cardiologico Monzino.
evidence.unknown: Improvement over the 4C score (the score was comparable); prospective performance; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A naive Bayes classifier selected features and produced the mortality-prediction score.
